#### **THROUGH THE VALLEY**

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/5ba549bd-1d39-4bdf-95d9-e4e258987b9b/JensenHuang_BigInterview_Photo_RyanYoun_Inline__1_.png?t=1794581533)
Caption: Image Courtesy: Ryan Young

**Nvidia’s first week without Jensen**

Just one big story today, because it’s the one everyone in AI is talking about.

Nvidia will be fine on Tuesday. It’s the next twelve months I’m less sure about.

If you missed it: [**Jensen Huang is out as Nvidia CEO after 33 years.**](https://apnews.com/article/f9ac67fed10c86c1ed1ad1f41dd921a5) (Still strange to type.) The man who turned a graphics chip startup into the company powering the AI boom resigned on Thursday, effective immediately, and left the board too. Nvidia has never had another CEO.

It follows reports of extramarital relationships, which Huang [acknowledged and apologized for](https://www.bostonglobe.com/2026/11/12/business/nvidia-ceo-resigns-heres-what-we-know/), and a national security question that is much harder to settle. That part centers on Alice Huang, who runs Megaspeed, a Singapore cloud company and Nvidia partner that has been [investigated over export-restricted chips reaching China](https://thehill.com/policy/international/6212857-alice-huang-spy-allegations-nvidia-ceo-relationship/). The New York Times reported that US intelligence [suspects she was working for Chinese intelligence](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/12/nvidia-megaspeed-alice-huang-jensen-.html).

Nothing has been proven. (Worth saying twice, given how fast this story is moving.) US officials say they’ve reached no conclusion, China denies it, Megaspeed says it followed the rules, and Nvidia’s board says it has [no reason to believe secrets or national security were compromised](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/09/megaspeed-nvidia-jensen-huang-alice-huang.html). Lawmakers say they’ll [keep asking about Nvidia’s China sales](https://www.technology.org/2026/11/13/jensen-huang-resigns-nvidia-ceo-colette-kress-interim/) anyway.

CFO Colette Kress, who has run Nvidia’s finances since 2013, is now [interim CEO](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001045810/000104581026000082/nvidiaannouncesceotransiti.htm) and keeps her old job too. The stock dropped more than 13% early Thursday, closed down about 4%, and [recovered on Friday](https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/live/nvidia-live-updates-following-jensen-huangs-resignation-as-ceo-allegations-of-a-third-affair-emerge-195535310.html).

Her first test is Tuesday, when Nvidia reports earnings five days into her tenure. I’ll be listening for three things: whether she commits to the chip schedule Huang laid out, whether Nvidia says anything new on China, and whether the board puts a timeline on finding a permanent CEO.

I’m calm about Tuesday because CUDA, the developer ecosystem and the demand for Nvidia’s chips don’t leave with Huang. The risk is slower. Big customers already wanted to depend less on Nvidia, and a leadership change gives them room to push. A year from now, I expect Nvidia is still the default for AI chips, with its biggest customers buying noticeably more from elsewhere, including their own.

Hold me to it.

Midjourney/Every illustration.

Was this newsletter forwarded to you? Sign up https://every.?ev_audience=free to get it in your inbox.



----------------------------------------



In June, we published the eight levels of AI adoption https://every.?ev_audience=free, giving people a map of where they are with AI today and what it takes to get to the next level. The map ran from Level 1, where you ask a chatbot a question, to Level 8, where a manager agent runs a team of subagents for you. I expected most readers to find themselves in the bottom half, and most of them did. What I didn’t expect was how quickly the people at the top would reach the end of the map.

Today, most engineers I talk to are running several long-running agents at once and handing the coordination work to an orchestrator. Even nontechnical teams are progressing faster than I thought they would, because the Codex and Claude desktop apps make orchestration much easier for knowledge work. As more people approach the top end of the eight levels we outlined in June, I keep getting asked, “What comes next?” My answer, which I covered in my talk at Thesis: 2027 https://every.

howdy, it’s Barsee again.

happy wednesday, AI family, and welcome back to AI Valley.

**here are the biggest things worth knowing today:**

* The AI 2027 researchers now think they were too conservative

* The Nvidia scandal makes no sense

* Plus trending AI tools, posts, and resources

Let’s _dive_ into the Valley of AI…


----------

----------
#### **ADOBE**

## [Adobe wants AI agents editing your creative projects](https://news.adobe.com/news/2026/11/adobe-firefly-expands)

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/24e5c33e-9735-4d3d-9f0b-99d5e30c331e/FF-AIA_PlanMode-Logo_3__1_.jpg?t=1794394443)
Follow image link: (https://news.adobe.com/news/2026/11/adobe-firefly-expands)
Caption: Courtesy: Adobe

Adobe Firefly, the all-in-one AI creative studio, is expanding the Adobe Creative Agent through new capabilities in Firefly AI Assistant (beta). It carries out multi-step tasks using Adobe Creative Cloud tools, including Premiere, Illustrator, InDesign, After Effects and [Frame.io](http://frame.io/), all guided by your direction. Describe what you want to make in your own words, then refine, redirect, or take over at any time.

Adobe is also previewing Adobe Creative Cloud MCP, a new way for creative professionals to direct third-party agents as they make changes directly inside native project files in Photoshop, Illustrator, Premiere and After Effects, while staying in control.

It's part of Adobe's approach to making pro-grade creative workflows easier to start, control and continue, wherever inspiration strikes.

[Explore what’s new from Adobe at MAX](https://news.adobe.com/news/2026/11/adobe-firefly-expands).

~_*This is sponsored_~


----------

----------
#### **THROUGH THE VALLEY**

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/ddedc056-7d08-4a65-9a6d-efb2cc83b8bb/image_-_2026-11-10T182505.958__1_.png?t=1794395108)
Follow image link: (https://ai2027tracker.com/)
Caption: Courtesy: AI 2027 Tracker

[**The AI 2027 researchers now think they were too conservative.**](https://blog.aifutures.org/p/q35-timelines-update-looks-like-the) All six authors of the famous [AI 2027](https://ai-2027.com/) scenario now expect a “superhuman AI researcher” sometime in 2027: AI as good as the very best human researchers, to the point where a lab would rather replace its entire research team than give up the AI. Daniel Kokotajlo now gives it a 50-50 chance by May 2027, pulled forward from December 2028 just three months ago. His own summary: [“I am scared, sad, and angry.”](https://x.com/DKokotajlo/status/2120204075803500595)

The reason is a [new METR assessment](https://metr.org/blog/2026-11-05-anthropic-ai-rd-acceleration-assessment/) of Anthropic. METR spent 11 weeks inside the company and estimates its AI progress is now running about twice its historical pace, with perhaps 80% of that speed-up coming from AI itself. The AI 2027 team says that puts us about five months ahead of their original scenario. Three months ago, even their most aggressive model gave less than a 4% chance of that happening by now.

If that sounds familiar, it’s because Anthropic warned in its [IPO filing](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2130357/000162828026068676/anthropicpbc-sx1ax1.htm) that AI might soon dramatically speed up its own research. That’s recursive self-improvement, or RSI: AI building better AI, which builds better AI still. METR’s report is the first serious outside evidence that the loop may already have started.

And this isn’t just engineers working faster. Anthropic staff self-report being 12x more productive with their latest internal model. METR’s finding is that the _whole company’s_ progress has roughly doubled, which is a much bigger deal.

**The forecasts that follow are wild: **Their model suggests 2027 alone could pack in something like five years’ worth of historical AI progress. They put a 35–65% chance on AI that beats top human experts at virtually all white-collar work arriving before 2028. And extrapolating Anthropic’s own automation data, they get 95% of its R&D tasks fully automated by November 2027. That won’t stay an Anthropic story. Whatever happens there will eventually happen at every lab.

One big caveat: Anthropic redacted most of the evidence METR relied on, and this is one company, so treat these numbers as a strong signal, not proof.

Still, what gets me is that the people whose literal job is forecasting this are the ones most surprised by it. If the pace is hard to take in for them, the rest of us probably aren’t taking it in at all.


----------

----------
# TRENDING TOOLS


--------------------
* [PaperTrades](https://papertrades.ai/?utm_campaign=aivalley) - watch Claude, Gemini and ChatGPT race with pretend money at real prices. Every trade, reason and grade is public. See who wins on Nov 28 ^~(sponsored)~^

* [Claude Whiteboards, Claude Sheets and Claude Data](https://x.com/claudeai/status/2120206365759094857?s=20) - think a plan through on a board, build a tracker in a sheet, and tell a story with your data

* [Businesses in ChatGPT](https://x.com/OpenAI/status/2120216592395174382?a=QNErUYjbOAew3svbCxI&s=20) - claim your business, manage your information, and get insights on how people engage with you

* [Google Gemini 4 Carbon](https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/models-and-research/gemini-models/gemini-4-carbon-now-available) - its strongest model, built for long agent jobs like coding, research, and security work
